text:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: SEV2 elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/streaming/* in us-east-1 gateway. Auto-escalation to on-call in 2m. Alert ID: ALRT-98821 :rotating_light:

maria-ops: saw it, joining. are we seeing client cancels or gateway returns?

ajay-sre: initial look -> spike of 502/504s + intermittent ECONNRESET on edge logs. lots of short-lived connections.

kevin-frontend: customers started reporting partial responses then closed sockets. sample user report: "stream just stops and client sees 0 bytes for a few secs then closes"

luis-backend: tailing gateway logs now. pattern: chunked transfer streams where the gateway emits `chunked: last` then connection closes with `RST`. I can paste a few lines:

luis-backend: ```
2026-03-14T21:12:34.123Z gateway-03 INFO conn=0x7f4a reset after write: write: broken pipe
2026-03-14T21:12:34.124Z gateway-03 WARN upstream=runtime-12 502 read: unexpected EOF
2026-03-14T21:12:34.125Z gateway-03 DEBUG stream-session id=abc123 frames=12 last-frame: true client-cancel=false
```

maria-ops: customer impact? which tenants / routes?

emma-support: I've triaged support tickets. ~18 customers in last 20m for chat streaming; top impacted are two SaaS customers on dedicated pools but hitting hosted gateway for routing (they're in us-east-1). No billing issues reported yet, just degraded UX.

ajay-sre: hypothesis1: gateway process hitting backpressure and forcibly closing upstream socket. hypothesis2: client-side cancels + gateway not propagating properly leading to double-close race. Need to check kernel TX queue / keepalive latency.

maria-ops: quick mitigation options?

ajay-sre: short-term mitigations: 1) enable streaming-fallback flag to force paged responses for affected route 2) scale gateway pool and bump internal connection limits 3) enable aggressive keepalive on gateway to avoid half-open sockets.

kevin-frontend: can we do 1) immediately? feature flag exists: `streaming.force_paged.v1` gated by route pattern.

luis-backend: I'm +1 on flag and scaling. We should also capture tcpdump on one gateway to confirm FIN/RST patterns. I'll request ephemeral capture on gateway-03.

maria-ops: assign tasks:
- ajay: scale gateway pool + monitor health metrics (latency, open fds, tx queue)
- kevin: flip streaming.force_paged.v1 for /v1/streaming/* in us-east-1 to true (targeted)
- luis: tcpdump capture and collect unusual kernel logs
- emma: prepare customer comms (ack + ETA)

ajay-sre: scaling now. bumped gateway autoscale target from 6 -> 12 instances in us-east-1 via deploy-bot. running: `/infra autoscale gateway us-east-1 12`

deploy-bot: Command received: `/infra autoscale gateway us-east-1 12` -> scaling initiated (request id: scale-7622). Expected new instances in 90-150s.

kevin-frontend: flipping flag now in feature-store UI -> `streaming.force_paged.v1` set to true for tag `us-east-1:streaming-route`

kevin-frontend: flag toggled. applying rollout for 10s -> 100% in 30s.

luis-backend: tcpdump started on gateway-03. capturing 60s window. saving to s3://redwood-dumps/incident-1719005123/gw03.pcap

maria-ops: monitoring customer-facing metrics: streaming success rate, average streamed tokens, 5xx rate.

(30s pass)

ajay-sre: new gateway instances healthy. connection backlog per-instance dropped from 320 -> 80. 5xx rate falling but still above baseline.

(60s pass)

kevin-frontend: after flag flip, some sessions are now paged. support reports that pages are coming through reliably. streaming success rate improved from 82% -> 94% for routed traffic.

emma-support: sending initial note to affected customers: "We're aware of streaming interruptions in us-east-1 and have temporarily disabled streaming for affected routes while we investigate. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for full restore."

ajay-sre: pcap shows many connections where client sends FIN after last chunk, gateway sometimes sends RST shortly after. Kernel tx_queue is non-empty at RST time in ~30% of samples -> suggests gateway worker crashing or force-close. investigating process-level OOM/segfaults.

luis-backend: checked logs, one gateway has repeated `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address` traces just before restart. instance id gw-03-7.

maria-ops: oh that explains RST. which binary? release tag?

luis-backend: gateway image `redwood/gateway:2026.03.11-rc4`. I see a libc error + stack. sending full stack to S3.

ajay-sre: mitigation: cordon the faulty instances from LB and drain. disabling `gw-03-7` now from router group to avoid restarts affecting live connections. `/infra drain instance gw-03-7 --grace 30s`

deploy-bot: Command received: `/infra drain instance gw-03-7 --grace 30s` -> draining (request id: drain-4432).

ajay-sre: also rolling back to `redwood/gateway:2026.03.07-stable` for us-east-1 fleet while we root-cause RC4 crash. Initiating canary -> then full rollout if stable.

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy: gateway us-east-1 -> image `redwood/gateway:2026.03.07-stable` (canary 2 instances). request id: deploy-8811.

kevin-frontend: can we keep streaming forced paged until stable is verified? I recommend keeping flag ON for at least 2 hours while we validate.

maria-ops: agreed. keep it on and add a follow-up ticket for postmortem and codefix PR.

emma-support: updating customers with ETA ~2h for full restore. adding note about workaround: they can use non-streaming endpoints which are unaffected.

ajay-sre: new canary instances look healthy. we are seeing memory footprint stable and no panics in canary logs for the new image. will wait 10m then continue rollout.

(10m pass)

ajay-sre: full rollout complete. monitored metrics: 5xx rate back to baseline within 3m of rollout. streaming success for those still on paged routes remains high.

luis-backend: uploading crash traces and diffs to ticket ENG-5809. suspected root cause: regression in buffer reuse that exposed nil pointer in high-concurrency path.

maria-ops: incident summary (short):
- root cause: regression in gateway release `2026.03.11-rc4` causing occasional panics under high streaming concurrency leading to RST/502 for streaming clients.
- customer impact: partial streaming interruptions for ~18 customers in us-east-1 for ~35 minutes. degraded UX; no data loss.
- mitigation: 1) feature flag forced paged responses for affected routes 2) scaled and drained faulty gateway instances 3) rolled back gateway to stable image 4) kept flag on until stability verified.

maria-ops: follow-ups:
- ENG-5809: fix buffer reuse + unit tests for streaming stress (owner: luis)
- ENG-5810: add better graceful shutdown to gateway worker to avoid RST on restart (owner: ajay)
- OPS-117: add alerting for gateway panics and rapid restart rate (owner: maria)
- COMM-44: customer incident postmortem draft (owner: emma)

emma-support: I'll draft the customer-facing postmortem and share in #support for review.

ajay-sre: any other asks?

kevin-frontend: once fix and canary pass, we'll flip `streaming.force_paged.v1` back to false and monitor. prefer a staged rollback by 10% increments.

maria-ops: thanks all. closing the live incident channel in 30m after we confirm no regression. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident ALRT-98821 acknowledged closed by maria-ops at 2026-03-14T22:03:09Z (duration ~51m).
